analysis: Two small changes were examined. (1) EngineV2KVQuantizationPolicy.swift lines 81-91: for Flint models the provider-wide `global` selection is no longer consulted, so the checkpoint default (balanced) does not trigger flintRequiresNative. Environment and per-model selections that are not native are still refused (lines 84-87), and the function still returns .native for Flint. This narrows an availability failure and does not weaken the precision restriction. The non-Flint path at line 90 still uses global. (2) EngineV2Factory+BackendPreparation.swift lines 180-183 and 224-228: for FlintModel, kvBackend `.auto` is promoted to `.paged`. That disables the crash-loop guard (line 215 requires kvBackend == .auto) and the degradesPagedFailure fallbacks (lines 329 and 341), which treat explicit paged as non-degrading. A hard refusal at line 224 is added if the backend resolves to anything other than paged, for example via the model_capability or kill_switch vetoes. Net effect: Flint fails closed instead of silently running on the contiguous backend. This is a fail-closed change with no confidentiality or integrity regression. Flint load can now fail where it previously fell back, a bounded availability trade-off; the crash-loop guard is bypassed for Flint, which could repeat a crashing paged path. That is an operational concern, not a security finding under the threat model. T-041 (prefix cache) is not affected. Quantized Flint is refused, and precision is native, so resident-prefix and hybrid-cache gating (lines 450-456) are unchanged. Unverified, because the code is outside the supplied evidence: the FlintModel type, the pagedUnavailable error handling by callers, and whether the Flint paged qualification claim holds. Nothing here changes coordinator-to-provider crypto, attestation, or key handling.
